subject: Business
title: What Is a Nudge?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is a Nudge?.

hook.text: A fly etched inside a urinal at Amsterdam airport reduced spillage by 80%. Nobody was forced to aim.

buildup.text: A nudge changes behavior by altering the environment, not by restricting choice or adding incentives.

discovery.text: Thaler and Sunstein popularized the concept: make the desired behavior the easiest path.

twist.text: Nudges are invisible by design. If you notice the nudge, it's probably not working as intended.

climax.text: Cafeterias that put salads at eye level and desserts in the back increase healthy eating — no bans needed.

punchline.text: Don't tell people what to do. Make the right thing easy.

quiz.question: What makes a nudge different from a mandate?
options: It changes behavior without restricting freedom of choice

details.summary: A nudge is any aspect of choice architecture that predictably alters behavior without forbidding options or significantly changing economic incentives. Examples include placing healthy food at eye level, setting default printer settings to double-sided, and simplifying enrollment forms.
details.whyItMatters: Nudges offer low-cost, high-impact interventions for businesses and governments. They improve outcomes by working with human psychology rather than against it, achieving behavioral change without mandates, bans, or expensive incentive programs.
takeaways: Nudges alter behavior without restricting choice or changing incentives
They work by aligning choice architecture with natural human tendencies
Effective nudges are simple, low-cost, and easy to opt out of

faq.question: What makes something a nudge rather than a mandate?
faq.answer: A nudge preserves complete freedom of choice. Banning sugary drinks is a mandate. Placing water at eye level and sodas on the bottom shelf is a nudge. The drinks are equally available but the choice environment makes the healthier option easier to select.

faq.question: What are the most effective types of nudges?
faq.answer: Default settings are the most powerful because most people never change them. Simplification of forms and processes removes friction from desired behaviors. Social norms messaging shows people that most of their peers engage in the behavior. Timely reminders prompt action at decision points.
